text:
sara.k: heads-up — saw weird CSV row/column scrambling in the structured-export test after rolling the hybrid quant build (GPTQ baseline + AWQ packing). small % of rows had fields swapped, reproducible.

mike.t: ugh. which test? the tablex multi-row exporter? :eyes:

sara.k: yeah tablex/csv/multirow. repro steps: temp=0, top_p=1, greedy decode, seed=42. deterministic but result order shifts on the quantized binary.

chen.l: can you paste an example diff? quick is fine.

sara.k: sure — original vs quantized output (cropped):

```
orig:
id,name,qty
1,apple,10
2,banana,5
3,carrot,12

quant:
id,name,qty
1,apple,10
2,carrot,12  <-- row 3 moved into row 2 spot
3,banana,5
```

sara.k: note: tokens look intact, it's the ordering of rows/columns sometimes swapping for multi-row generation.

eva: did you run GPTQ-only and AWQ-only? need to bisect.

sara.k: ran quick sweep overnight:
- gptq-only: no swaps in 2k rows
- awq-only: 1.4% swaps
- hybrid (gptq base + awq packer): ~0.9% swaps

mike.t: interesting that AWQ shows more. might be a packer/permute issue in output projection or a kv-cache boundary problem leaking between rows.

chen.l: can you repro locally with small script? share the request body you used.

sara.k: posted curl snippet:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-hybrid-001","prompt":"<csv spec>...","format":"csv","max_tokens":80,"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"seed":42}'
```

chen.l: running that now on gpu. also trying CPU for contrast.

ci-bot: CI build 2130456700 (quant-pack-v4) finished: all tests green except flaky/tablex-csv (1 failure) — see https://ci.redwood.ai/2130456700

mike.t: quick checks — diffed logits for final token positions between fp32 and awq on a few examples. there's a divergence that changes argmax for the token representing newline vs comma in ~0.7% cases.

chen.l: newline vs comma edge-case could reorder fields if generator decides to end a row early. any seed/beam differences?

sara.k: we force greedy so beam/seed not the cause. also observed row-swap in models that produce explicit row indices (so it's not just punctuation).

eva: thoughts: 1) check AWQ packer for output-head permutation bug 2) KV-cache alignment across batched prompts (multi-row generator uses streaming micro-batches) 3) check tokenizer mapping of special tokens (newline/comma) in the quantized vocab table.

chen.l: doing a tight bisect: will rebuild packer with a no-permutation debug flag to emit raw indices. also running the mini-benchmark with kv_cache disabled.

mike.t: FYI I reproduced a swap on a tiny local sample. when I disabled continuous-batching it went away. so kv-cache/microbatch look likely.

sara.k: nice — that aligns with the microbatch theory. maybe rounding in AWQ causes subtle timing/length differences that let one batch's tail leak into the next when caches are reused.

chen.l: test results so far (quick):
- awq + continuous-batching: swaps ~1.2%
- awq + batching-disabled: swaps ~0.01%
- gptq + continuous-batching: swaps ~0.0%

eva: actionable then: 1) put a short-term mitigation to isolate streams (disable microbatching for tablex exports on hybrid models) 2) fix long-term: audit AWQ packer cache reuse paths + add unit for kv-cache isolation.

ci-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1234 — "AWQ: microbatch kv-cache isolation bug leading to row reorder in structured outputs"

sara.k: I'll roll a canary config to disable continuous-batching for `redwood-hybrid-001` on tablex routes and monitor.

mike.t: add a telemetry gauge for 'row-order-violations' in tablex test harness so we can measure impact.

chen.l: I'll keep digging into packer and post a PR with assertions to fail if output-proj indices don't match fp32 reference. linking draft when ready.

eva: thanks team. good triage. cc @platform for any routing/opt impacts.

sara.k: thanks — will update thread after canary runs. :+1:
